Hi Jordan — quick technical write-up to address your questions. I attached a short sample SDK config (sample_sdk_config.yaml) and an example response schema. Key points below.

1) Auth modes supported- API keys (simple, bearer header)- OAuth 2.0 (client credentials + token refresh)- mTLS (client certs) — supported for Dedicated/Private deployments; Hosted supports OAuth + API keys; mTLS available for Private by default.

2) Chat vs Completions token accounting- Token budget is per-request and counts all tokens sent to the model: system + user + assistant history + prompt.- max_tokens is the model-side generation cap (how many tokens the model will emit). If total tokens (input + max_tokens) exceed model limit, requests will be rejected.- For multi-turn chat, you should truncate/prefix history on the client or use our conversation APIs that manage summarization.

3) Stop sequences & streaming semantics- Stop sequences are applied server-side and will terminate generation; with streaming (SSE/delta frames) you will still receive token deltas up until the stop is applied.- To avoid partial JSON/structured-output fragments in streaming, we recommend:
  a) Use function-style/tool-calling (we support a 'functions' schema that returns a single function call payload) — that is sent as a final discrete object when the model decides to call the function.
  b) OR stream plain text and finalize with a final 'completion' that contains the structured JSON in full (i.e., do optimistic streaming for UX but fetch the final JSON when the model completes).

4) Structured output / tool calling- Our SDK supports a functions-like schema (name + JSON schema). The model will either emit a function call (structured) or normal text. Function calls are delivered as a single atomic event (less risk of broken JSON), and we include a separate field in the response payload for the function arguments.

5) Embeddings & reranker- Recommended model: redwood-embedding-1 for vector generation.
- For real-time reranking, do an online embedding for the user query and do an approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search over precomputed doc embeddings, then optionally rerank the top-K with a cross-encoder style re-score using an instruction tuned model.

6) SDK details / attachments- sample_sdk_config.yaml shows auth examples + routing to a dedicated pool (if you want predictable latency).- rsp_schema_example.json shows a structured response with a top-level 'tool_call' block we recommend for actionables.

If you can share your sample payload, we can produce a concrete example request/response mapping and a short integration checklist. Happy to cover these on the 8/24 call.

Thanks,
